title: Erasmus+ MotivAction
excerpt: ATTP members took part in a working meeting on fighting and preventing manipulation at sporting events
body_html:
For the first time in the Republic of Moldova, this week saw a two-day seminar of the PNIS (National Platform for Integrity in Sport), held as part of the international MotivAction project.

This exceptional seminar, held at the Moldovan National Teams Training Centre, was attended by Corentin Segalen, chair of the Group of Copenhagen at the Council of Europe and coordinator of the French National Platform, and Patrick Vajda, a specialist in risk management at sporting events, a former international fencing referee and president of the International Federation of Sports Officials.

Our team, Setka-Pro Moldova (ATTP), was represented by Oleg Dobrjinschi, Master of Sport and President of TOP CUP Academy; Veniamin Dubrovin, Master of Sport and performance coach; and Serghei Cucerovschii, Master of Sport and top-category referee. The seminar was intended to discuss and analyse all the problems and challenges encountered in sports competitions, especially the match-fixing incidents found in table tennis around April 2022. A practical, effective tool tailored to athletes’ needs will then be developed to encourage reporting of manipulation and to help implement whistleblowing policies at national level.

The transnational MotivAction project brings together representatives of national anti-manipulation platforms, sports organisations and groups of international experts.

They will work together to develop mechanisms that motivate athletes, referees and coaches to report situations of
manipulation. In total, the project’s activities are expected to reach an estimated 30,000 people involved in sports competitions.

As part of the fight against manipulation in sports competitions, our team’s representatives were accredited by the European
Commission (Erasmus+ Sport) to take part in the transnational MotivAction project alongside experts from 7 other countries:
Bulgaria, Cyprus, France, Greece, Portugal and Poland.

Note that the National Platform for Integrity in Sport is made up of the National Anti-Doping Agency, the Ministry of Education and Research, the Ministry of Internal Affairs, the Anti-Corruption Prosecutor’s Office, the National Anticorruption Centre, the Intelligence and Security Service, the Service for Preventing and Combating Money Laundering, the Public Services Agency, the National Lottery of Moldova, the National Tennis Federation of the Republic of Moldova, the Moldovan Basketball Federation, the National Association of Professional Table Tennis Players of the Republic of Moldova, the Wrestling Federation of the Republic of Moldova, the Mixed Martial Arts Federation of the Republic of Moldova and the Moldovan Football Federation.

Project objectives:
- Consulting sports stakeholders and national platforms.
- Gathering and understanding the views, needs and circumstances of the sports stakeholders involved (athletes, referees, coaches) on existing issues around whistleblowing and manipulation.
- Consulting the organisations that make up the national platform on whistleblowing tools and policies.
- Encouraging dialogue within the national platform on reporting in sport.
- Adapting and creating effective reporting tools at national level.
- Implementing national whistleblowing policies to promote, protect and manage alerts against the manipulation of
sports competitions and to encourage reporting of manipulation.
- Working together to better understand how to motivate athletes, referees and coaches to report manipulation.
- Drawing up and implementing national action plans for effective reporting mechanisms and whistleblowing policies
at national level.

Creating a trusted, effective and secure reporting mechanism is essential for the reporting process to be seen as positive by athletes and clubs as well as by local authorities.

In this respect, MotivAction will be a legal and operational laboratory for improving the monitoring capacity of National Platforms and the mechanisms for detecting anomalies, thereby safeguarding the integrity of
sports competitions.

ATTP continues to step up its efforts to protect the integrity of table tennis and, in cooperation with the relevant international organisations and partners, has adopted a zero-tolerance approach to all forms of manipulation and/or
illegal influencing of matches.
